emergency.whenToCall: Call when someone is seriously injured or needs urgent medical help, or when life or property is in immediate danger.
emergency.whatToSay: Say which service you need: police, fire or ambulance. Stay calm and give your location.
emergency.mobileNote: From a mobile phone you can also dial 112. It connects to the same services. If there is no mobile coverage on any network, you cannot reach Triple Zero.
emergency.appNote: The free Emergency+ app can show your GPS location to read out to the operator if you do not know where you are.

tips.title: Crocodile attack
steps: Call 000 immediately.
Move away from the water's edge.
Press firmly on any bleeding wound with a clean cloth.
Keep the person still until help arrives.

tips.title: Snake bite
steps: Call 000 and ask for an ambulance.
Keep the person still. Do not let them walk around.
Put a firm bandage over the bite, then wrap up the whole limb and splint it.
Do not cut the bite, suck out venom, use a tourniquet or wash the area.

tips.title: Jellyfish sting (box jellyfish, Irukandji)
steps: Call 000, or get a lifeguard to help.
Pour plenty of vinegar over the stung area for at least 30 seconds. Do not use fresh water.
If there is no vinegar, pick off any remaining tentacles.
Start CPR if the person is not breathing normally.
Get urgent medical care.

tips.title: Heatstroke and extreme heat
steps: If you suspect heatstroke, call 000 and ask for an ambulance.
Move the person to shade or a cool place and lay them down.
Cool them down: wet the skin, fan them and put cold packs on the neck, armpits and groin.
Give cool water only if the person is fully alert and able to swallow.

sources.name: healthdirect: Hot weather risks and staying cool

tips.title: Bushfire
steps: Call 000 if a fire threatens life or property.
Follow the advice of the fire service and local emergency alerts.
Leave if you are told to evacuate.
In NSW you can also call the Bush Fire Information Line on 1800 679 737.

sources.name: NSW Rural Fire Service: Total Fire Bans factsheet

tips.title: Caught in a rip current
steps: Stay calm and float to save your energy.
Raise an arm and call out for help.
Swim parallel to the beach or towards the breaking waves until you are out of the rip.
